newsitem.title: CHINA: Triplenic buys hotel interest in China.
newsitem.headline: Triplenic buys hotel interest in China.

text.p: Hong Kong property group Triplenic Holdings Ltd said Friday it had agreed to purchase Fu Hui Holdings Limited's 50 percent stake in Hungexpress Investment Ltd for HK$180 million.
In a statement, Triplenic said it would issue 41.62 million new shares at HK$4.325 each to Fu Hui Holdings in exchange for the stake in the investment holding group.
Through the purchase, Triplenic will gain a 25 percent attributable interest in Hungexpress' sole holding, the Silver Star Hotel Ltd of Shanghai, which operates the Holiday Inn Crowne Plaza Shanghai.
The four-star, 495-room hotel is 50 percent owned by Shanghai Film Development General Co.
In the 1996, Silver Star posted HK$24.01 million in pretax profit on sales of HK$163.67. This compares with pretax profit of HK$45.23 million on sales of HK$170.44 in 1995.
Its net asset value at the end of 1996 was HK$675.74.
Triplenic said the dilution effect on earnings due to the new share issue would not be material.
"The directors consider that the acquisition will supplement the hotel interest in Xiamen, Fujian province which the group newly acquired earlier this year," Triplenic said.

"In line with the group's corporate strategy of penetrating into the hotel industry and property development and investment in China, the directors will continue to pursue other suitable investment opportunities," it added.
So Sik, chairman of both groups, and his associates own about 61.7 percent of Triplenic and 18.1 percent of Fu Hui.

Fu Hui said the move marks its exit from the hotel business and leaves it free to concentrate on its wholesale, retailing and industrial businesses. "It is expected that a surplus over the net book value of Hungexpress of approximately HK$4 million will be generated on completion of the disposal," it said.
